title: Beauty Industry Trend Report - July 2026
description: From radiant body glow to playful fruit-inspired nails, explore the beauty trends defining July 2026 and how brands can tap into authentic social content.

blocks.x: TRENDS LIVED-IN MAKEUP, BODY GLOW, FRUITY NAILS
TRENDS LIVED-IN MAKEUP, BODY GLOW, FRUITY NAILS

Perfection is taking a backseat this summer. Across TikTok and Instagram, creators are moving away from perfectly polished beauty in favor of looks that are effortless, expressive, and distinctly personal. The content gaining momentum is about enhancement, celebrating texture, movement, and individuality through small but impactful details. From lived-in makeup and radiant skin to playful nail art, July's trends reflect a broader shift toward beauty content that's authentic, approachable, and inherently social.

The era of perfectly placed contour and pristine makeup is beginning to soften. This summer's defining aesthetic is "lived-in makeup” - a look that appears naturally worn, slightly blurred, and effortlessly cool. The effect is makeup that looks naturally lived in rather than freshly finished.

According to Who What Wear, consumers are gravitating toward beauty that embraces texture, movement, and imperfection instead of masking it. Creator Maggie Aubrey is leaning into intentionally softened finishes that are authentic rather than overly polished while Brittany J aka Bora Blueprint wants her makeup to look like she “just woke up from a nap.”
For brands, the opportunity lies in showcasing lightweight, skin-first formulas and content that celebrates authenticity, movement, and real-life wear.

Radiance is moving beyond the face. This summer, body glow has become an essential finishing step, with illuminating oils, shimmering lotions, and skin-enhancing balms creating healthy-looking luminosity from head to toe. The effect is subtle rather than sparkly - a lit-from-within glow that complements minimal makeup and sun-kissed skin.

Glamour recently identified body glow as one of this summer’s defining beauty trends, highlighting the shift toward soft, reflective finishes over obvious shimmer. Helping fuel the movement is excitement around Rhode’s Highlight Milk Luminizer which has quickly become a favorite among creators for its skin-like radiance and luxurious finish. Across TikTok and Instagram, creators like Addy Kate are incorporating illuminating body products into their GRWM routines, applying glow to shoulders, collarbones, legs, and décolletage as the final step before an evening out.

As beauty routines extend beyond the face, brands have an opportunity to elevate body care through premium textures, sensorial application, and lifestyle-driven storytelling. Products that deliver believable radiance while fitting seamlessly into everyday routines are well positioned to drive both engagement and trial.

This summer's manicure trend is very playful. From tiny cherries and citrus slices to strawberries, blueberries, and peaches, fruit-inspired nail art is adding a dose of personality to beauty routines without feeling overly complicated. According to Vogue, fruit nails have emerged as one of the season's standout manicure trends, reflecting consumers' appetite for beauty that feels joyful, expressive, and inspired by summer rituals. Rather than intricate maximalist nail art, today's designs are clean, colorful, and intentionally whimsical.

Across TikTok and Instagram, creators like Angelika and Hey Great Nails are doing in-depth tutorials around fruit-inspired manicures as a fun way to personalize their look, pairing minimalist nail shapes with playful seasonal details that feel instantly shareable.

The popularity of fruit nails highlights consumers' desire for small moments of creativity within otherwise pared-back beauty routines. For brands, the opportunity lies in tapping into seasonal storytelling and creating content that feels playful and approachable.

July's beauty trends suggest consumers are placing greater value on how beauty feels than how perfectly it's executed. Content that appears effortless, relatable, and emotionally resonant is increasingly outperforming highly polished production, reflecting a broader desire for authenticity across social platforms. For brands, the opportunity is to create content that feels more human, whether that means lived-in looks or playful whimsy. The beauty looks capturing attention this summer aren't striving for perfection; they're inviting participation.
